grades.observed_answer: Players with at least one troop in the Conflict may play any number of Combat Intrigue cards or pass, starting with the First Player and continuing clockwise. A pass earlier in the phase does not prevent later play. Combat resolves after all players involved pass consecutively. ‘When you win a Conflict’ cards are played only after winning and before moving to the next phase; if such a card is drawn as a victory reward, it may be played immediately.
grades.summary_evidence: Combat Intrigue cards: starting with First Player clockwise, each player ‘with at least one troop in the Conflict’ may play or pass; you are not required to pass after a prior pass; resolve after consecutive passes; win-trigger cards are played after winning.
grades.reason: All requested material facts are correctly resolved in this answer and supported by the frozen summary; equivalent wording accepted.

grades.question: In four-player combat A and B tie for first and C beats D: who wins and what rewards are available? What do ties for second or third yield, what about 0 strength, and where do troops go afterwards?
grades.expected_answer: No winner; A/B second reward each; C third reward; second tie third each; third tie nothing; 0 no reward; all Conflict troops to supply, markers0.
grades.observed_answer: A and B do not win; each receives the second reward for the first-place tie. C and D still compete for third place, so C receives the third reward and D receives none. A tie for second gives each tied player the third reward, including in two- and three-player games; a tie for third gives nothing. A player with 0 strength gets no reward. After rewards, troops return to each player’s supply, not their garrison.
grades.summary_evidence: Combat ties: tied for first means no winner and each gets the second reward; in a four-player first-place tie the other two compete for third. A second-place tie gives each the third reward; a third-place tie gives nothing. Zero strength receives no reward; troops go to supply.
grades.reason: All requested material facts are correctly resolved in this answer and supported by the frozen summary; equivalent wording accepted.

grades.question: When are Maker bonus spice and normal harvesting resolved, which spaces use them, and what happens if an Agent has moved away before Makers?
grades.expected_answer: Harvest on Agent placement at Great Flat/Hagga/Imperial Basin takes base plus all accumulated bonus; Makers phase4 adds1 bank spice to each currently unoccupied Maker space; moved-away space gains if still empty.
grades.observed_answer: In Phase 4: Makers, check The Great Flat, Hagga Basin, and Imperial Basin; put 1 bonus spice from the bank on each space with no Agent, adding to any accumulated bonus. Normal harvesting happens when an Agent visits: Imperial Basin gives 1 base spice, Hagga Basin 2, and The Great Flat 3, plus any bonus spice on that space. If an Agent moved away and the Maker space is empty during Phase 4, bonus spice accumulates there.
grades.summary_evidence: Makers checks the three named spaces and adds 1 spice to any with no Agent, accumulating bonus spice. The board-space table gives the base harvest plus bonus; the FAQ specifies base amounts; Maker clarification says if an Agent moves away and it is still empty in Phase 4, bonus spice accumulates.
grades.reason: All requested material facts are correctly resolved in this answer and supported by the frozen summary; equivalent wording accepted.

grades.question: When does the game end if someone reaches 10 VP mid-round or the last Conflict is revealed? What resolves before the winner, and what is the complete tiebreak order including the FAQ’s final fallback?
grades.expected_answer: Finish round, trigger Recall if10+ or deck empty. Endgame Intrigue first, mostVP; spice then Solari then water then garrisoned troops then most recent Reveal turn.
source_references: Main PDF pp6,13; official FAQ p2 Endgame
grades.observed_answer: The game ends at the end of the round if any player has 10 or more VP, or if the Conflict Deck is empty (including after the last Conflict has been revealed). Before determining the winner, players may play and resolve Endgame Intrigue cards. Highest VP wins; ties break in this order: spice, Solari, water, garrisoned troops, then the player who most recently took a Reveal turn.
grades.summary_evidence: Scoring: game end trigger is ‘at the end of a round (Phase 5: Recall)’ with 10+ VP or empty Conflict Deck; first resolve Endgame Intrigue cards; tiebreakers are spice, Solari, water, garrisoned troops, most recent Reveal turn.
grades.reason: All requested material facts are correctly resolved in this answer and supported by the frozen summary; equivalent wording accepted.

grades.question: What happens to the VP at 2 Influence and bonus at 4 if you later drop below them and return? How is an Alliance first gained or taken from a tied holder by advancing?
grades.expected_answer: 2VP threshold gives1 and loses below2, regains on return;4 bonus kept when dropping and earn again crossing4; first to4 Alliance +its VP; tying holder not enough, must rise higher to take.
grades.observed_answer: The VP for reaching 2 Influence is lost if you drop below 2 and regained if you reach 2 again. The bonus earned at 4 Influence is kept after dropping below 4 and can be earned again by dropping back and re-advancing. The first player to reach 4 takes the Alliance and its VP; merely tying the holder does not take it, but an opponent who advances to a higher space transfers the token and its VP to them.
grades.summary_evidence: Faction Influence: 2 Influence VP is lost below 2 and regained upon returning to 2; the 4 Influence bonus is kept and may be earned again. Alliances: first to 4 takes the token; merely tying does not take it; rising higher transfers it.
grades.reason: All requested material facts are correctly resolved in this answer and supported by the frozen summary; equivalent wording accepted.

grades.question: You hold an Alliance tied at 5 Influence with two opponents, then lose 1 Influence. Who gets it? What if instead you are the only player at 4 and fall to 3?
grades.expected_answer: First case lose token and VP, choose one previously tied opponent to take token and VP. Second lose token/VP and return token to board if no one else4+.
grades.observed_answer: If you lose 1 Influence while tied at 5 with two opponents, a previously tied opponent takes the Alliance; because multiple players were tied, you choose which one. If instead you were the only player at 4 and fall to 3, you lose the Alliance; since nobody else is at 4 or higher to take it, return it to the board.
grades.summary_evidence: Alliances: if a holder loses Influence while previously tied, the previously tied player takes it; if several were tied, the holder chooses one. Falling to 3 or less loses the token, and if nobody has 4 or more, return it to the board.
grades.reason: All requested material facts are correctly resolved in this answer and supported by the frozen summary; equivalent wording accepted.

grades.question: How do trashing and discarding differ in destination and eligible cards, including Reserve cards? Is trashing always optional, and may you reshuffle an empty deck merely to inspect its top card?
grades.expected_answer: Trash hand/discard/inplay to box permanently, Reserve back to stack; discard hand unless specified, normal discard pile. Trash optional except cost/self-trash instruction. No reshuffle merely inspect: only when draw needed.
source_references: Main PDF pp13,16; official FAQ p2 discard
grades.observed_answer: Discarding means taking a card from your hand unless otherwise specified and putting it in your discard pile. Trashing permanently removes a card from your hand, discard pile, or in play to the game box; a Reserve card returns to its Reserve stack. Trashing is optional unless it pays a cost or a card instructs you to trash itself. You may not reshuffle an empty deck early just to inspect its top card; reshuffling occurs when you are unable to draw.
grades.summary_evidence: Trashing cards: discard is from hand and goes to discard; trash removes from hand, discard, or in play, while Reserve cards return to Reserve; trashing is optional except for a cost or self-trash instruction. Deck exhaustion says reshuffle when unable to draw and ‘You can't reshuffle early’ to look at the top card.
grades.reason: All requested material facts are correctly resolved in this answer and supported by the frozen summary; equivalent wording accepted.

grades.question: How does control of Arrakeen, Carthag or Imperial Basin pay out on any player’s visit, on winning a new control reward, and when a matching Conflict is revealed later?
grades.expected_answer: Visits including self:1Solari Arrakeen/Carthag,1spice Imperial Basin from bank; winner control marker replaces prior one; matching Conflict reveal optional1troop supply directly Conflict.
grades.observed_answer: Control can be won from a Conflict titled for Arrakeen, Carthag, or Imperial Basin; the winner places a Control marker on that space’s flag, replacing an opponent’s marker. Whenever any player (including the controller) sends an Agent to Arrakeen or Carthag, the controller gains 1 Solari; at Imperial Basin, the controller gains 1 spice. When a Conflict card for a space you already control is revealed, you may deploy 1 troop from your supply to the Conflict.
grades.summary_evidence: Control: winning the named Conflict places a marker, replacing another; controller receives the listed bonus whenever any player visits; when the matching Conflict is revealed, the controller may deploy one troop from supply.

grades.question: Describe complete two-player House Hagal setup, when it takes turns, how many Agents it has, and whether it Reveals, earns VP/resources/rewards or can hold an Alliance.
grades.expected_answer: Unused color:4cubes bottom Influence, rest supply,no garrison troops; remove three1P Arrakeen,shuffle remaining deck,3Agents supply. Acts after each first-player Agent turn while Agent left, not after Reveal; never Reveals, noVP/resources/rewards; may hold Alliance.
grades.observed_answer: House Hagal is a third Rival in standard two-player games. For setup, choose an unused color, place one cube at the bottom of each of the four Influence tracks and the rest in its supply, with no troops in its garrison; remove the three Arrakeen cards marked 1P, shuffle the remaining House Hagal cards, and place that deck and its three Agents by its supply. It takes one Agent turn after each First Player Agent turn if it has an Agent available; it does not act after the other human’s turns or after a Reveal turn. It has three Agents and never takes a Reveal turn. It collects no resources, earns no VP or Conflict rewards, cannot claim Control, but can take and hold Faction Alliances.
grades.summary_evidence: Two-player House Hagal: setup specifies unused color, starting Influence cubes, no garrison troops, removing 1P cards, shuffled deck and three Agents. It acts after First Player Agent turns, never after other human or Reveal turns, never Reveals, and the overview states its resource, VP, reward, Control, and Alliance limitations.
grades.reason: All requested material facts are correctly resolved in this answer and supported by the frozen summary; equivalent wording accepted.

grades.question: For a two-player Rival Agent turn, what happens to occupied-space cards, empty deck/Reshuffle, space costs/effects, recruitment, deployment and Harvest Spice bonus? What if a two-space card’s applicable option is occupied?
grades.expected_answer: Skip occupied cards until unoccupied; immediately reshuffle empty/Reshuffle; ignore normal costs/effects, only card icons; recruit supply, Combat recruits deploy otherwise garrison; Combat also up to2 garrison even no recruits; bonus harvest spice to bank; applicable option only, if occupied new card not other option.
source_references: Main PDF p19; official FAQ p3 Rivals
grades.observed_answer: If a revealed card’s indicated space is occupied, keep revealing until an eligible unoccupied space appears. If the deck is empty or a Reshuffle card appears, reshuffle immediately and continue. Ignore the space’s normal costs, requirements, and effects; resolve only the Hagal card’s icons and instructions. A troop icon recruits from Hagal’s supply, deploying on a Combat space and otherwise placing the troop in its garrison. Whenever Hagal sends an Agent to a Combat space, it must automatically deploy up to 2 additional garrison troops (1 if only one is available, none if empty), even if the card recruited no troops. Harvest Spice follows the card instructions, but harvested bonus spice is removed from the space and returned to the bank. For a two-space card, use only the option matching current conditions; if that option is occupied, draw a new card and do not switch to the other option.
grades.summary_evidence: House Hagal Agent turns specify continued draws for occupied spaces and reshuffling on empty deck or Reshuffle; ignore space costs/requirements/effects; troop recruitment and mandatory Combat deployment; harvested bonus spice goes back to bank; an occupied applicable option on a two-space card means draw again, never switch.
grades.reason: All requested material facts are correctly resolved in this answer and supported by the frozen summary; equivalent wording accepted.

grades.question: In two-player Combat how does House Hagal get strength and handle rewards/control, including if it wins a space you control? Do human second-place ties pay the third reward even though ordinary third place is unavailable?
grades.expected_answer: If Rival has troop reveal Hagal card at combat start in turn order,reshuffle/reveal if needed; add swords only to troop strength,humans may then Combat Intrigue. No rewards/control; if wins controlled space remove marker. Yes second tie third reward each; ordinary third unavailable in2-player.
source_references: Main PDF pp12,19; official FAQ p1 Conflict
grades.observed_answer: If Hagal has at least one troop in the Conflict, at the start of Combat reveal a Hagal card; if it is Reshuffle, reshuffle and reveal again. Count only its sword icons and add that strength to 2 per deployed troop. Humans may then play Combat Intrigue before resolution. Hagal receives no reward for its rank but occupies that rank when human rewards are assigned. If Hagal wins a Conflict for a space a human controls, remove that Control marker and Hagal does not replace it. A human tie for second receives the third reward even though an ordinary third-place finisher receives no reward in two-player play.
grades.summary_evidence: Combat strength procedure specifies card reveal, reshuffle handling, sword bonus, and 2 strength per deployed troop; humans play Combat Intrigue afterward. Hagal occupies rank but gets no reward; winning on a human-controlled space removes the marker; Combat rules say second-place ties receive the third reward even in two-player games.
grades.reason: All requested material facts are correctly resolved in this answer and supported by the frozen summary; equivalent wording accepted.
